payload.description_html:
The Mississippian limestones of the Mammoth Cave region formed at the bottom of a shallow saltwater sea now known as the Mississippian Sea around 300-330 million years ago. At that time, MACA would have been a great place to come for a snorkeling vacation. The park was about 4 degrees south of the Equator. Think, the Bahamas, but much warmer and with more sharks!

According to the labels here[1], the taxa depicted are from top left to right Glikmanius, Saivodus, Kalops, Cladodus, Stethacanthus.
